hook_text: In 1859 a man was hanged in Virginia. Half the country cheered. In the other half, church bells rang in mourning.
clip_script: His name was John Brown, a white farmer who believed slavery was a sin so terrible it had to be destroyed by any means. He lived among free Black farmers and treated them as equals, rare for a white man then. In Kansas, his group killed five pro-slavery men. Then, in October 1859, he and twenty-one men, Black and white, seized the government armoury at Harpers Ferry, hoping enslaved people would rise up. Within two days, Marines stormed his hideout. He was tried and hanged. The South called him a terrorist. Many in the North called him a martyr. Historians still argue. But within two years the Civil War had begun, and by 1865 slavery in America was over.
visual_style: A whiteboard gallows silhouette at dawn, the country map split in two with cheering on one side and ringing bells on the other; a small brick engine house surrounded by soldiers; a newspaper headline reading Slavery Abolished 1865.
pacing: Divided-nation hook, a quick life story, an open question at the end.
